passedScope.assessment: The vector resultant F1 is spring force plus weight, not spring force alone. Two equal liquid-film interfaces each exert F; F1=-2F expresses opposite directions. One-interface cases do not inherit the factor2.
Positive downward h expands the film; quasistatic external-resultant work A=F1h=2Fh is positive. Friction/viscous losses and changing force are excluded; weight is not counted twice.

Initial/final S1/S2 denote one face area; equal two-face energies include factor2. Fixed-condition reversible surface work is correctly distinguished from generic internal-energy change. The source n-shaped descriptive energy subscript remains a native authoring blocker, not a physics variable change.
Once the area difference is corrected, A=2sigma lh and2Fh=2sigma lh give F=sigma l per interface. Full film force is twice this for the stated symmetric two-interface setup.

Force is locally tangential to the interface and normal to its boundary; vector directions matter on curves. l is the wire-contact length, not full frame perimeter. J/m2 equals N/m. Appendix values remain source-attributed and condition-dependent, without fabricated data.
Both figure objects and captions retained in source order. Actual new figure gate remains pending; this SCI does not claim pixel approval.

findings.assessment: S1 is initial single-face area and S2 final area. A positive downward displacement h of a wire of length l increases area by lh, so S2-S1=lh. Printed reversed order contradicts the immediately preceding A=2sigma(S2-S1) and following positive A=2sigma lh. The honest draft warning does not make a completed lesson with an unresolved equation.
